locator.text: Equation (10.8), p. 119, in the proof of Lemma 10.2

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No declaration was found stating either majorant in the physical variables (r,τ): the powers r^{-1-2h-2j} and ρ^{-3-4h-2j} do not occur in the repository (searches listed below found only the j = 0 exponent -1-2h, in LocalHeatFormula.lean:70 and RenormalizedHeatMoment.lean:428/467). The Lean takes a different route to the same conclusion: instead of estimating K and K²/ρ in ρ with a j-dependent power, it factors the radial powers out exactly first. `BaseExterior.heatCoefficient_sq_scaled` (BaseExterior.lean:391) and `heatPressure_formula` rewrite the tail integral as -(C²/2)·s^{-2A}·heatPressureFactor h ν with s = r²/2, ν = (1-t)/s, A = 1/2 + h, after which only the dimensionless variables (ν,v) are estimated: `heatJet_bound` bounds every ν-derivative of the profile uniformly for v ≥ 1 (the factor (2/v)^n inside `heatJet` plays the role of the paper's r^{-2j}), and `heatPressureJet_dominated` supplies the single dominating function v ↦ v^{-2-2h}·B for every ν-derivative of the dimensionless pressure density. Under s = ρ²/2 the paper's second majorant integrates to the same weight — ρ^{-3-4h}dρ = (2s)^{-2-2h}ds, and -2A-1 = -2-2h — so the two majorants control the same integral, but the Lean's is uniform in the derivative order j while the paper's carries ρ^{-2j}. The paper's use of (10.8) (dominated convergence justifying ∂_τ^j p^loc(r,τ) = -∫_r^∞ ∂_τ^j(K(ρ,τ)²/ρ)dρ up to τ = 0) is reached as `heatPressureFactor_contDiffOn` and `BaseExterior.heatPressure_contDiffOn_closed`. I did not trace whether the Lean's smoothness route is used at exactly the point of Lemma 10.2 where the paper invokes (10.8).
